Review Text:
Aarif Fort is the oldest historical building in Hail city. It was built to protect the city from enemies. During Saudi rule, the fort was used for moon sightings and iftar cannon firing during Ramadan. Recently, the A'arif Fort was opened to tourists as a cultural heritage site.
Fort Aarif is a rectangular shaped castle that is built with mud and clay. It is located in the heart of Hail and was built in the 17th century AD. The fort occupies an area of about 440 square meters and is strategically located on top of a hill, making it visible from every point of the city. Located on top of Jabal Irf, the fort offers a magnificent view of the northern city.
The fort can be accessed through a gate on its southern side, where a small courtyard leads to the main entrance. Inside the fort you will find observation towers, windows, a living area, baths, a mosque and storerooms.
This castle is also notable for its large wooden doors with inscriptions engraved on them. Tourists can climb to the top of the castle to get a bird's eye view of the city and observe the farms, markets and neighborhoods around them.

Review Text:
The Qishlah or Al-Qishlah is a palace in the center of the city of Ha'il, Saudi Arabia. It was built in the 1940s as an artillery and weapons depot during the reign of Prince Abdulaziz bin Musaad Al Saud of Hail province. It is a two-storied mud palace, 142.8x141.2 meters, its walls are 8.5 meters high and there are eight watch towers along with the walls with two main gates, east and west.
Qishlah comes from the Turkish word for fortress or barracks (Kışla). The purpose of its construction is to become a central location for army units arriving there. It was then a prison until the end of bin Musaad's reign, when it was re-designated as a historical building by the government.
The Qishlah fortress was made a landmark in 1995.

Review Text:
Pros:
- Excellent rates. Shown room prior to paying for it.
- Friendly staff with an English speaking female present, she was very pleasant to deal with! (I'm a female visitor commenting).
- There is a supermarket and clothing stores nearby. Its a good all round centralised location.
- Round the clock shuttle service, returning you to the hotel also!
- We were upgraded rooms without additional charge. Room was presented to us in a clean state with AC, safe box and a fridge present. Spacious double bed, most comfortable bed I've ever slept on! Wow!!!!! And I've travelled to many places.
- Masjid within the hotel leading prayers if unable to make it to the haram. Imam has a beautiful voice. Good prayer space.

Just some notes of concern, nothing major:
- No, haram is not within walking distance. With the Shuttle bus you are dropped off to Al Ghazza bus station (B Gate 2 > pick up from same location), 20 minute walk to the haram. Eventually all that walking strained my feet along with the heat/fatigue & hotel room AC affecting my health (barely 30 years old - healthy female), towards the end we kept taking taxi directly to King Abdul Aziz Gate (I put down Al Marwa by Rotana hotel on Careem/Uber then instructed driver towards that gate). Charge about 10-15 SAR on app. Private taxis WILL charge excessively unless you haggle (though private taxis carry safety risks). Maybe you can manage on shuttle, give it a go! Very reliable and saves you tons.
- Shuttle bus & taxi equally take about 10 mins to get there.
- Elevators are a nightmare to go up and down with, especially as we were at the top floor (20). Gets packed easily with other hotel guests, all different nationalities. 8 elevators yet they all get crammed. Very nice seeing people of all backgrounds within the hotel lobby however.
- Have data on hand, WiFi is not so reliable. They were prompt with giving the password though.
- Shuttle bus return also easily gets packed out, just beware. Can't complain though because its a fantastic free initiative to facilitate worshippers to and from the haram. Just ensure to set out an hour before the designated prayer time.
- Have your own cleaning products on hand to give the bathroom sink a quick scrub every now and then. We didn't receive room service and to be honest I didn't want my things moving about so no issue with that. Overall hotel hygiene rating would be 7/10.

Hope I've been as thorough as I could to help others decide, no regrets choosing this hotel for my first umrah. Thank you!

Zam Zam means "Stop Stop". It is a well in masjid Al Haram some 20 meters away from Kaaba. Normally a well is dried up after 70 years in that Saudi soil but zam zam is giving water since last 5000 years.

At this point this water source streamed up under the foots of Hazrat Ismaeel by the will of Allah to quench his and his mother's thurst.

Prophet Muhammed (peace be upon him) said: “May Allah bestow mercy on Ismail’s mother! Had she left the Zamzam flow without trying to control it, Zamzam would have been a stream flowing on the surface of the earth.”

Please note that before our Prophet Muhammad’s grandfather, Abdul Muttalib, and many years after him, the flow of Zamzam water abated and later completely blocked. Abdul Muttalib received a vision in sleep to re-dig the well, and so he located the well and dug it for it to start pumping again and feed the pilgrims. This became the process carried out by Abdul Muttalib’s family and his son Abbas Bin Abdul Muttalib inherited this responsibility after him.

Shopping malls have become more than just places to shop; they’re entertainment hubs, social gathering spots, and even cultural experiences. Whether you’re searching for the latest fashion trends, a delicious meal, or simply a fun day out, a visit to a shopping mall can offer something for everyone. From bustling city centers to serene suburban landscapes, malls cater to diverse needs and preferences, making them a fascinating reflection of modern life.
Exploring the Mall Experience
What draws people to these colossal structures? It’s the promise of a diverse range of experiences all under one roof. Imagine strolling through air-conditioned comfort, browsing through a myriad of shops, catching the latest blockbuster, and enjoying a delectable meal, all without stepping outside. This convenience and variety are key to the mall’s enduring appeal. For families, malls offer a safe and engaging environment for children to play and explore while parents relax. For tourists, they provide a glimpse into local trends and consumer culture.
Are you looking for that perfect outfit for a special occasion? Malls house a wide array of clothing stores, from high-end designer boutiques to affordable fast-fashion outlets. Whether you’re after traditional Indian attire or international brands, you’re likely to find it within the mall’s sprawling corridors. The ability to compare prices, try on different styles, and receive personalized service adds to the allure of the in-person shopping experience.
Dining and Entertainment Options
Beyond retail therapy, malls offer a plethora of dining and entertainment options. Craving authentic Indian cuisine? Many malls feature food courts brimming with diverse culinary delights, from spicy street food to elegant fine dining. For movie buffs, multiplex cinemas offer the latest releases in a comfortable setting.
Looking for some family fun? Many malls incorporate entertainment zones with activities like bowling, arcade games, and even indoor theme parks. These spaces provide a welcome escape from the daily grind and offer a chance to create lasting memories.
Navigating the Mall Maze
While the sheer size and variety of a mall can be exciting, it can also be overwhelming. A well-structured map and clear signage can help you navigate the maze of corridors and locate your desired shops and amenities. Many malls also offer digital directories and mobile apps to further enhance the visitor experience. Don’t hesitate to ask mall staff for assistance; they are usually well-versed in the layout and can provide helpful directions.

Review Text:
Museum Al Wahyu, also known as the Hira Cultural District, is a significant cultural and religious site located at the base of Jabal Nur in Makkah, Saudi Arabia. This museum offers visitors an immersive experience into the history of Islamic revelations, particularly focusing on the moment Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) received the first revelation in the Hira Cave.

Location and Significance
Situated approximately 4 kilometers northeast of the Masjid al-Haram, the museum stands at the foot of Jabal Nur, the mountain that houses the Hira Cave. This cave is historically important as the place where Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) received the first revelation from the Angel Gabriel. The museum's location allows visitors to connect deeply with this pivotal event in Islamic history.

Exhibits and Features
Opened in early 2023, Museum Al Wahyu spans over 67,000 square meters and utilizes advanced technology to present its exhibits. Visitors can explore interactive displays and multimedia presentations that narrate the stories of various prophets, from Prophet Adam to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon them all). A notable feature is the life-sized replica of the Hira Cave, enabling guests to visualize and feel the environment where the first revelation occurred. The museum also offers 3D animations and large-scale screens that depict significant moments from Islamic history, enhancing the educational experience.

Visitor Information
The museum operates daily with two sessions: from 8 AM to 2 PM and from 4 PM to 12 AM. Admission fees are 20 SAR for adults and 10 SAR for children. Guided tours are available in multiple languages, including Indonesian, ensuring a comprehensive understanding for international visitors. To reach the museum from Masjid al-Haram, visitors can take a taxi or bus, with the journey typically lasting around 15 to 20 minutes.

Future Developments
Plans are underway to construct a cable car system connecting the museum to the Hira Cave. This initiative aims to provide easier access for visitors wishing to reach the cave, which currently requires a challenging hike up Jabal Nur.

In summary, Museum Al Wahyu offers a profound and educational experience for those interested in the origins of Islamic revelations. Its strategic location, combined with state-of-the-art exhibits, makes it a must-visit destination for pilgrims and tourists in Makkah.

This may be because we were on the 9th floor but I wanted a high floor for the view so it’s a trade off I was happy with. Finally the parking is more than enough. There are plenty of spaces outside but they are not covered. There is also basement parking but it’s a little tight to manoeuvre, especially a big car/truck. During my stay there was plenty of space to choose from but during busy periods it may be an issue. But there will always be somewhere you can find outside. To my knowledge there is not valet parking. Overall I would definitely recommend and I would definitely return in the future.

Review Text:
Pros:
This is a very nice hotel and it is very well priced. The interior and exterior are clean, the hotel has nice curb appeal and the staff is friendly and attentive. The hotel is in an area with a lot of construction going on, but there is plenty of shopping and restaurants within walking or driving distance.

I stayed in a Jr. Suite, which was very large; it included a seating area with a very comfy sofa and other chairs, as well as a flat screen tv. There are numerous electrical outlets throughout the room and all of the outlets are the standard 3 prong 220 outlets, but they are the design that allows for US style plugs to be inserted (just be sure that your appliances/devices are 220 capable before doing so!)

The bedroom is a separate room, which is very nice and has it's own AC unit, which was a nice touch, as well as it's own large flat screen TV.  There is an iron, ironing board, coffee station and refrigerator in the bedroom.
The bed is very comfortable, large and outfitted with extremely comfortable sheets and blankets.
There is a very nice breakfast buffet and room service is available 24/7. The food that I had was very tasty and was delivered quickly ans as described in the menu.

Now for the Cons: Every hotel has a few of these, and aside from a couple that really stood out, the rest are small and miniscule, but noteworthy for your planning or info.

Parking:::: There is NO ON-property parking. There is a small strip mall, on the west side of the hotel. Depending on how busy those shops are will determine whether you get a spot. There is a bank on the east side of the hotel, but you cant park there for fear of being towed. There is a small parking lot behind that bank, but park at your own risk. There is very little lighting back there, so I wouldn't leave valuables in the car. I was told by hotel staff that I could park there, but found a spot in the strip mall.
-There is no safe in the room. Not a huge deal, but it would be a nice addition.

-In the Jr. Suite, there is what appears to be a small "kitchenette" area, but it is only a counter and some cabinets. Perhaps the addition of some plates/cutlery and a hotplate would be nice. I would suggest moving the refrigerator, which is the bed room to this area. Otherwise, it is a wasted space.

--The bathroom is on the small side and oddly enough, there’s  a tub instead of a shower with no curtain, which means that water inadvertently goes everywhere. There are only two towels in on the rack, and there was no floor towel.
A minor annoyance is the fact that the shower floor is raised by about 6 inches from the floor in the hall, so I tripped a few times when entering the bathroom or kitchen area.
Again, these are all very minor issues that should in no way take away from this hotel. It’s a great place and very well priced. If I happen down to the area again, I would definitely consider staying there again and would definitely recommend it to friends.

Extremely Disappointed with Mark & Save – Poor Customer Service, Improper Handling & Rigid Policy Over Common Sense

I had a very frustrating and disappointing experience with Mark & Save, and I believe it’s important to share it so others are aware of how poorly customers can be treated when things go wrong—even if the mistake is on the store’s part.

On 28th March 2025 at 2:10:31 AM, I made a purchase at one of their branches. While checking out at the billing counter, some items were scanned and billed, but not handed over to me. I trusted that everything was packed properly, so I didn’t double-check at that time. It was only when I returned home and reviewed my purchase that I noticed the missing items.

This was already a frustrating realization, but what followed was even worse. Since Eid started on 30th March, I was tied up with family and religious commitments and was genuinely unable to return to the store within their stated 3-day return/exchange policy. However, I went back as soon as I could, expecting that the staff would at least acknowledge the circumstances and assist in resolving the issue, especially since:
•	I had the original receipt with the exact date and time of purchase
•	The mistake was clearly on the part of the staff who failed to hand over scanned items
•	It was a genuine oversight that could have easily been verified via CCTV or internal records

To my shock, I was met with completely unhelpful and unprofessional behavior. The staff didn’t even make an effort to check what happened or verify my claim. They simply kept repeating that the 3-day policy had passed, and that nothing could be done—even though I tried explaining my situation patiently and respectfully.

Not only was my concern dismissed, but it was handled with a complete lack of empathy, flexibility, or accountability. No manager stepped up to support or even apologize for the inconvenience caused by their team’s error. It was clear that the priority was following the policy blindly, rather than providing proper customer service or attempting to resolve an issue caused by their own mistake.

Policies are important, yes—but good customer service means being able to apply them with common sense, especially during national holidays like Eid when customers might genuinely be unable to return immediately. Refusing to even investigate the claim or acknowledge the issue shows that Mark & Save is more interested in protecting themselves than serving their customers.

I walked away from this experience feeling cheated, unheard, and disrespected, despite being a paying customer with valid proof and a fair request. I will not be returning to Mark & Save, and I strongly advise others to be cautious when shopping there. Always double-check your bags before leaving, because if something goes wrong—even if it’s their fault—you’ll be on your own.

When the scorching desert sun sets, only then does the city arise from its slumber. We were fortunate enough to visit here during a cultural festival. We were entertained by bag-pipe-and-drum music from Oman, games display, live music and much more. The well-maintained little cubicle stands were filled with local hand crafters, a magnificent sculptor, grass matt basket weavers, a drum maker, wooden products, jewelry sellers and many more. The local cuisine was exquisite, and I had the best tea of my life sitting under a date tree with the dates hanging overhead.
It was refreshing to see families having clean, decent traditional fun without any alcohol, with the well-behaved children playing outside and not sitting on their cellphones the whole time and made us feel nostalgia for our own childhood.
The traditional house museum was fantastic and gave us insight into how families function and live.
The date exhibition tent was pure heaven for me. I have never seen dates in so many configurations for sale under one roof. It was brilliant to see local people supporting local industry and farms.
The art exhibit was well-organized, well-displayed and well-curated and 90% of the display was created by local artists. It was a real treat.
But by far the best experience for us as South-Africans was the generosity, openness, hospitality, kindness and interest shown to us. We were approached by many to warmly welcome us to their beautiful country. We felt special and appreciated. Thank you kindly for that.
Al-Asha is a magical place with the friendliest people I have met anywhere in Saudi-Arabia and the 4 days we had to spend here was not nearly enough to experience all it has to offer.

Review Text:
Beautiful location, well appointed rooms and the food is superb. We really enjoyed our stay, but some advice follows to manage your expectations, mitigate frustrations and optimize your trip from day one.

The quality of service simply does not match the price point, so perhaps don't over spend on the room as you'll feel short changed. Plenty of other reviews remark on this. Whilst some of the staff are very good, it's visibly inconsistent and annoying when you have to ask repeatedly for things or for instance have your request for a taxi forgotten about, or are brought the wrong drink again. This is really just a factor of it being a busy hotel with a lot of guests and many more staff. Workers I expect have a high turnover and do not appear to be managed in such a way as to engender a sense of teamwork and care for the holistic experience. On a few occasions I noticed the gardeners taking photos of the work they had just completed, suggesting these were then being sent to "command" to prove they were competing their chores.

Villas 1-10 are too close to reception, so ask for another if allocated one of these.

Having a bike is a game changer. Ask for one on day one. When free they'll bring to your room and you can keep for your stay. Its a long walk uphill to the restaurant or gym and really hot during the day (April). The buggies will always pick you up either from the room or enroute, but it's far more enjoyable being independent.

The restaurant and pool during the day are incredibly busy and worth avoiding. The spectacle of tiktok'ers filming themselves walk by the pool is funny at first, then rather tiresome. Far less of an issue in the morning and evening.

Breakfast starts at 7am and is more enjoyable at this time before it gets really busy. You'll get served quickly and fewer mistakes on your order. However, worth knowing it really does run until 11am and they were still topping up the buffet at this time. Therefore, if you can get back from your morning trip, you needn't miss out.

The transport organized by the hotel is far too expensive and just unnecessary. Our hotel pickup also drove terribly and having asked if music was ok, then played loud house music, kept skipping around and replaying tracks. We chanced on an AlUla taxi driver MD Faruuk Ali who was totally prompt and dependable. Used him for day trips and the airport run for a fraction of the price.

The above needn't dissuade you. I'm pleased we went and would still recommend. Hopefully this info helps you make the most of your trip.

We were looking forward to our trip here and we booked our stay with Caravan AlUla by Our Habitas.  When we checked into our Caravan (number 110) at around 4plus pm on 27 March 25, we were briefed by the receptionist about all the wonderful things we can do in both Caravan AlUla by Our Habitas and Our Habitas AlUla. We were told that the swimming pool will close at 9pm during check-in at 4pm and hence we took our time to settle down in our caravan and happily drove over to Our Habitas AlUla close to 6pm for an evening sunset swim. Upon reaching the pool at around 555pm, a female staff at the entrance of the pool asked for our room number and my wife told her we don’t stay here but at the Caravan site instead and gave her our caravan number. When we asked for towels, a male staff by the name Moshin came over and told my wife that the swimming pool will close at 6pm during the Ramadan month. My wife still clarified with him that our Caravan reception staff told us that the pool closes at 9pm but he insisted that the pool closes at 6pm during Ramadan. Being an understanding hotel guests, we abided by the hotel’s rules and shrugged off the missed opportunity to have a sunset swim. Instead we decided to just enjoy the surroundings with picture takings. But during the 50 mins we were there, other guests continued to stay in the pool even after 6pm and new guests even entered the pool and provided with towels around 6:30pm. Puzzled , we asked the other  male staff who gave out the towels “why is swimming still allowed after 6pm” and his reply was “these guests were not cooperative and insisted on swimming but he had alerted the security” yet 30mins passed and no security came and when we left at 7pm, they were just getting out of the pool. To show our displeasure at rules being enforced on different guests, we expressed our thoughts and comments to the male staff who handed out the towels and sensing out displeasure, he offered damage control by offering us to swim in the pool anytime now and offering us drinks and even alerted the Tama restaurant’s manager who was higher level. He furthered offered damage control like free dinner and even offered to lay out the sunbeds for us to swim before or after dinner which we politely turned down as our happy holiday moods at that moment already vanished and replaced with utter disappointment. All these damage controls were commendable but it came too late amidst our enthusiastic holiday mood to enjoy our stay at Habitats being dampened pretty much. Will think twice about recommending Habitas to friends as staff’s information consistency is apparently shockingly lacking. Such minor details can make or break a guest “experience” and yet Habitas emphasise so much on their “guestexperience@habitasalula.com” review. This bad aftertaste guests experience is really memorable in an extremely bad level.

Hegra also known as Mada’in Salih. 'Cities of Salih'), is an archaeological site located in the area of Al-'Ula within Medina Province in the Hejaz region, Saudi Arabia. A majority of the remains date from the Nabataean Kingdom (1st century AD). The site constituted the kingdom's southernmost and second largest city after Petra (modern-day Jordan), its capital city.Traces of Lihyanite and Roman occupation before and after the Nabatean rule, respectively, can also be found.

The archaeological site lies in an arid environment. The dry climate, the lack of resettlement after the site was abandoned, and the prevailing local beliefs about the locality have all led to the extraordinary state of preservation of Al-Hijr, providing an extensive picture of the Nabatean lifestyle. Thought to mark the southern extent of the Nabatean kingdom,Al-Hijr's oasis agriculture and extant wells exhibit the necessary adaptations made by the Nabateans in the given environment.                                                                                                                      its markedly distinct settlement is the second largest among the Nabatean kingdom, complementing that of the more famous Petra archaeological site in Jordan.The location of the site at the crossroads of trade, as well as the various languages, scripts and artistic styles reflected in the façades of its monumental tombs further set it apart from other archaeological sites. It has duly earned the nickname "The Capital of Monuments" among Saudi Arabia's 4,000 archaeological sites.

The Quran places the settlement of the area by the Thamudi people during the days of the prophet Salih, between those of Nuh (Noah) and Hud on one hand, and those of Ibrahim (Abraham) and Musa (Moses) on the other. According to the Quran, the Thamudis were punished by God for their idolatry, struck by an earthquake and lightning blasts. Thus, the site has earned a reputation as a cursed place—an image which the national government is attempting to overcome as it seeks to develop Mada'in Salih for its potential for tourism.

In 2008, UNESCO proclaimed Mada'in Salih as a site of patrimony, becoming Saudi Arabia's first World Heritage Site. It was chosen for its well-preserved remains from late antiquity, especially the 131 monumental rock-cut tombs, with their elaborately ornamented façades, of the Nabataean Kingdom.

Review Text:
Makan Indian Restaurant: From Zero to Hero!

So, picture this: two years ago, I strolled into Makan Indian Restaurant full of hope, only to leave feeling like I’d just attended a culinary tragedy. The food? Meh. The supervisor? More of a “cheerleader for chaos” than an actual leader. I mean, who knew a restaurant needed a traffic cop?

Fast forward to today, with Maharaja Restaurant out of the picture, I thought, “Why not give Makan another shot?” Spoiler alert: It’s like they flipped a switch and decided to impress me!

First up, the lentil soup. It was so earthy I half-expected a squirrel to join me for lunch. Seriously, it was rich and comforting, like a warm hug from Mother Nature herself—if she were serving soup, that is.

Then came the Dahi Poori. Crispy, refreshing, and a burst of flavor! It was like a party in my mouth, and everyone was invited!

Now, let’s talk about the vegetable samosas. The stuffing was fantastic, but the dough? It was so thick I thought they were trying to build a samosa fortress! I was half-expecting a “samosa workout plan” on the menu.

I ordered two lamb biryanis: one spicy and one not. When the spicy one arrived, I tasted it and thought, “Is this supposed to be spicy or just practicing its sass?” I told the staff, and they whisked it away like it was a contestant on a cooking show, and when it returned, it was on fire! Now that’s customer service!

But the real star of the show was the Bhuna Ghosht. Oh my goodness! The meat was cooked to perfection—tender, flavorful, and so rich that it could’ve won an Oscar for “Best Supporting Role in My Dinner.” Every bite was a delight, and I might have even considered proposing to my plate.

A huge shout-out to Ashish, my superb waiter! He was like the superhero of the dining room—always there, cape not included, making sure my dining experience was smoother than a Bollywood dance move!

Oh, and let’s not forget the ambiance! They had this lovely background music called “Bahon Ke Darmiyan (Unwind Instrumental)” by Jitendra Thakur & Amar Khandha playing. It was so relaxing that I almost forgot I was at a restaurant and not in a spa. If only the mixed grill had been as calming. It had potential, but it was so overcooked it could have auditioned for a role in a dry meat documentary. They were like, “We tried our best, but we’re just too overachieving!”

Overall, Makan has made a comeback that deserves a round of applause (and maybe a gentle reminder about the grill). If you’re looking for delightful dishes that might just make you forget your past grievances (and the occasional dry meat), this place is worth a visit! Cheers to second chances! 🍽️✨

I must say it left quite an impression! I decided to go for the B Burger Double, paired with their classic fries, and the experience was nothing short of satisfying.

The B Burger Double was incredibly flavorful. The beef patties were cooked to perfection—juicy, tender, and seasoned just right. The buns were soft but firm enough to hold the burger together, and the toppings—fresh lettuce, cheese, pickles, and sauce—elevated the taste without overpowering the beef. Every bite was a burst of flavor, and the double patty was a great choice for anyone who loves a heartier burger. Plus, at around 60 SAR for the burger and fries, the price felt reasonable for the quality and portion.

As for the fries, they were the perfect complement to the burger. Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, they weren’t too oily and had just the right amount of seasoning. Simple yet delicious, they provided that classic burger-and-fries combo that always hits the spot.

Beyond the food, the vibes at Section-B were fantastic. The place has a relaxed, modern atmosphere with a cool, minimalist design. The lighting, music, and overall ambiance made it a great spot to unwind and enjoy the meal. Whether you’re there with friends or just looking for a quick bite, the environment really adds to the whole experience.

Review Text:
I recently stayed at this hotel for three days, and while there were some positive aspects, a few key issues need improvement for a better guest experience.

Bathroom:
The bathroom design was quite problematic. The triangular shape, combined with a half-glass panel, caused water to spread all over the floor while taking a bath. This made the bathroom messy and uncomfortable to use. Installing a sliding glass door instead of the half-panel would be a much better solution to prevent water from splashing out.

Room Service:
The hotel should maintain a proper standard for room service, including daily room cleaning and bed arrangement. During my three-day stay, no one came to clean the room or organize the bedding. When I asked customer service about it, I was told that cleaning happens every morning, but this was not the case.

The hotel administration should take note of these issues, as they create a very poor impression. Improving these aspects will greatly enhance the overall guest experience.

Thanks
M Zahid
London - UK

A Disappointing Experience Despite the Beautiful Setting.

Me and my wife visited this restaurant in Madinah after seeing the positive reviews and beautiful aesthetics on Google, thinking that an intercontinental menu would ensure a satisfying meal. There's no doubt that the place is visually stunning.

The biggest disappointment came with the "karak chai." As a Pakistani, this drink is a staple of my culture. Upon receiving it, I noticed powdered milk, which was already a red flag. The chai was overly sweet, so I requested one without sugar. The staff member argued that this is how they make their chai, and even suggested I make my own tea with Red Label. He repeatedly mentioned that the chai had already been served and I would be charged for it, despite me stating that I had no problem paying, but just wanted one without sugar. His frustration was evident, and he seemed angry throughout our interaction, which was very disappointing.

In the end, we paid the bill and left, feeling that while they got the aesthetics right, they completely missed the mark on customer service and the quality of the food.

There is only so much of Pizza Hut, KFC, McDonalds you can eat, and those places are not cheap. there's also no where to eat either, unless you take it back to the hotel. So came across this restaurant "City Owners Restaurant"-Pakistani Hotel.
What can I say?
Its very decently priced, clean, staff are very polite & friendly. They do veg dishes too, not just chicken, Mutton, Biryani dishes. They are open 24 hours too. They do breakfast, Lunch and evening meals. Fixed Menu for breakfast & a fixed menu for lunch & evening meal but plenty to choose from, you wont be disappointed.
What's more, is they do a beautiful cup of Dhesi Tea / Chai - Its tops!
They give a fair amount of food, Nans are free, so if you want more - no problem. You wait like 2/3 mins if that for your food.
They take cash or card too.
They do salad if you like too.
Service is excellent.

Also, I got to say, the food isn't heavy like the Pakistani Restaurants in the UK. I am from the UK, when I have Karahi's, Balti's, Korma's, It kind of unsettles my stomach for a couple of days -  I had non of this with this Restaurant at all. So, Go on give it a try & I will guarantee, you will be returning back again!

If you're feeling generous, buy a few extra food dishes & they will pack them up for you and Walk back towards the Haram & give them to the Haram workers as Lillah/Sadqah - The smile on their face is so rewarding, let alone the reward you will get in the hereafter.

Finally - where is this place ?
Find Gate No 330 & walk down straight, go past 2 blocks, when you see Concode Hotel, it's on the same road. If you are facing the Concode hotel, it's towards the Left of it.

Review Text:

Recently, my family and I visited Madinah which is one of the holiest cities in Saudi Arabia 🇸🇦 for muslims and we were on the lookout for a decent eatery to cozy into and simply enjoy our lunch before we head out for an afternoon stroll through the bustling streets of Madinah for some shopping. Unfortunately, I couldn’t take pictures of our dinner meals as we were so hungry and just got to eating it 😝.

Review Text:
I found this food street near Masjid An Nabawi on my last night in Madinah and wished I had discovered it earlier to try more options. The place is designed to take you on a culinary journey from Madinah to the world, with food stalls offering cuisines from across the globe. Here are the cuisines I tried 👇🏻

1️⃣ Lebanon 🇱🇧

I tried the Lamb Kabab and Shish Tawouk served over rice, with a side of salad and tahini-based sauces. I really enjoyed the Lamb Kabab, it had smokey flavors and traditional spices. However, the Shish Tawouk was a bit too salty, and some pieces were rubbery.

💰 Price: 34 riyals per dish.

2️⃣ Pakistan 🇵🇰

I had naan with mutton keema and white chicken curry. The mutton keema was decent, but nothing special. The gravy of the white chicken curry was incredibly flavorful and paired perfectly with the naan. However, I had an unpleasant experience with the service. After the server noticed we weren’t Pakistani, there was a noticeable shift in his behavior. While inquiring about some of the menu items that we seemed to be confused with, he spoke in an odd tone, asking things like, “You don’t know this? You don’t have this in Bangladesh?” and kept exchanging glances while smiling with the cashier, who also seemed to be in on some sort of joke. While packing our order, my mom asked for leg and breast pieces, and the staff indicated that he was giving us those cuts. But when we opened the package at our hotel, we discovered he had actually given us a different order, filled only with mostly bone pieces and barely any meat. Since we were the only ones ordering takeaway at the time, it seemed unlikely to be a simple order mix-up. It was disheartening to experience such behavior, especially in a holy city like Madinah. Although the chicken was flavorful, I won’t be returning due to the staffs’ actions.

💰 Price: 1 riyal for naan, 20 riyals for each main dish.

3️⃣ Syria 🇸🇾

I tried their Shawarma and Tulumba. The shawarma was okay, but I’ve had better ones elsewhere in Madinah, so it didn't stand out. However, the Tulumba was perfectly made — crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, with an extremely sweet flavor. Disclaimer: If you struggle with balancing sugar levels, it might be overwhelming.

💰 Price: 10 riyals for Tulumba, 15 riyals for a small shawarma.

I wish I'd found this place earlier; I only managed to try three cuisines this time. But inshaAllah, if the opportunity arises, I’ll come back to try the rest. Overall, it’s a great spot to enjoy a meal with your family after Isha prayers.

Review Text:
8/2/25, Saturday, 9am:

Gua Sajadah (also known as Gua Bani Haram or Gharr Al Sajdah), though it is not as widely documented as other Islamic historical sites. It is a cave in Bukit Sa'la (also spelled Jabal Sela) near Masjid Nabawi in Madinah, Saudi Arabia.

What is Gua Sajadah?
Gua Sajadah is believed to be a place where Rasulullah SAW prayed, sought solitude, and reflected. It is most famous for the event during the Battle of Khandaq when Muaz Ibn Jabal found Rasulullah SAW in deep, prolonged sujood, leading him to fear that the Prophet had passed away.

According to the story, Rasulullah SAW was in sujood after receiving a message from Angel Jibrail (Gabriel), who conveyed Allah’s greetings and asked what he wished for his ummah. The Prophet’s response, "Allah knows best," was followed by Jibrail returning with the reassurance that Allah would not forsake or disappoint him regarding his followers. In gratitude, Rasulullah SAW performed sujood for an extended time, which Muaz mistook for death.

Historical & Religious Significance
Connection to the Battle of Khandaq – The cave served as a resting and prayer place for Rasulullah SAW during the Ghazwah al-Khandaq (Battle of the Trench) in 627 CE. This battle was crucial in Islamic history, as it was when the Muslims defended Madinah by digging a trench to prevent the Quraysh and allied tribes from attacking.

A Place of Deep Worship – The prolonged sujood symbolizes extreme humility and gratitude to Allah. The story highlights how Rasulullah SAW always turned to Allah in times of distress and joy.

Spiritual Landmark – Though less known than Jabal Nur (where Hira Cave is located) or Jabal Thawr (which contains the cave where Rasulullah SAW and Abu Bakr hid during Hijrah), Gua Sajadah holds deep significance for those who know its story.

Current Status
Unlike other well-known Islamic historical sites, Gua Sajadah is not heavily promoted as a tourist or religious site. Over time, its location near Masjid Nabawi has become harder to access due to urban development. Some reports suggest the cave is now within restricted or private areas, making it difficult for visitors to reach.

Alhamdulillah, at the time of our visit, the place was accessible despite a signage inducating that the place us inside military zone . There were also not too many visitors.

**Jabal Uhud (جبل أحد)**
Located approximately 5 kilometers north of Medina, Saudi Arabia, Jabal Uhud is a striking red-hued mountain renowned for its profound historical and spiritual significance in Islam.  It derives its name from the Arabic word for "one" (أحد), reflecting its solitary presence amidst the landscape.

The mountain is eternally linked to the **Battle of Uhud (625 CE)**, where Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions faced the Quraysh of Mecca.  Despite initial success, a tactical error led to a challenging setback, resulting in the martyrdom of 70 Muslims, including the Prophet’s beloved uncle, Hamza ibn Abdul-Muttalib.  The battle symbolizes resilience, sacrifice, and the importance of unity and discipline in adversity.

Today, Jabal Uhud is a revered pilgrimage site.  Visitors honor the martyrs buried at its foothills and reflect on the lessons of the battle.  The Prophet (ﷺ) once expressed affection for the mountain, saying, *"Uhud is a mountain that loves us and is loved by us"* (Sahih al-Bukhari).  Its rugged terrain and serene vistas also attract those seeking both spiritual solace and natural beauty.

Jabal Uhud stands as a timeless testament to faith, sacrifice, and the enduring legacy of early Islamic history.

4. **Simple Yet Beautiful Architecture** – Though it has been expanded over time, it retains a serene and peaceful atmosphere.
5. **Located on the Outskirts of Madinah** – About 5 km from Masjid an-Nabawi, it is a key stop for pilgrims visiting Madinah.

“The Muslims said takbir, rejoicing at his arrival, and they went out to meet him… He continued until he stopped in Quba, among Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf, and he stayed among them for fourteen days, and founded the mosque of Quba, which is the first mosque to be established after the beginning of his Prophethood.”

The great scholar Muhammad al-Amin al-Shanqiti (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

“With regard to the order of building, al-Masjid al-Haram was the first mosque to be built for mankind. The mosque of Quba was the first mosque built by the Muslims. Al-Masjid al-Haram was built by Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and the mosque of Quba was built by the Seal of the Messengers (peace and blessings be upon him). The site of al-Masjid al-Haram was chosen by Allah and something similar may be said about the site of the mosque of Quba.” (Adwa al-Bayan, 8/326)

We do not know anything about its area when it was built. It is located south of al-Madinah, but its structure is recent and there is no trace of the first structure.

The Muslims paid attention to the mosque of Quba throughout the ages. It was renovated by ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), then by ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz. Other caliphs also expanded and renovated it, until the final expansion in 1406 AH.

The size of the prayer hall alone is now 5035 square meters, and the area occupied by the mosque with all its facilities is 13,500 square meters.

Virtue of praying in the mosque of Quba

There are hadiths from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) which speak of the virtue of praying in the mosque of Quba:

Al-Bukhari (1193) and Muslim (1399) narrated that Ibn ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to go to the mosque of Quba every Saturday, walking or riding.

According to a report narrated by Muslim, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to go to the mosque of Quba walking or riding, and he would pray two rak’ahs there.

Al-Tirmidhi (324) narrated from Usayd ibn Zuhayr al-Ansari, who was one of the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Prayer in the mosque of Quba is like ‘Umrah.” (Classed as sahih by al-Albani in Sahih al-Tirmidhi)
Al-Nasai (699) narrated that Sahl ibn Hunayf said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Whoever goes out to this mosque, the mosque of Quba, and prays therein, will have (a reward) like that of ‘umrah.” (Classed as sahih by al-Albani in Sahih al-Nasai)

As for the mihrab, there was no mihrab in it when it was first built. The scholars stated that the building of mihrabs in mosques began in the second century AH.

Atmosphere and Ambiance

The Ajdan Walk location embraces The Cheesecake Factory’s signature upscale yet welcoming vibe. The decor mixes classic elegance with modern comfort, using warm lighting, spacious seating, and unique architectural elements that create an inviting atmosphere. The restaurant is bustling yet well-spaced, giving diners a sense of privacy without losing the lively ambiance. The outdoor seating also offers a scenic view of the Ajdan Walk promenade, perfect for enjoying cooler weather in the evenings.

Menu Variety

The menu at The Cheesecake Factory is famously extensive, featuring a wide range of American-inspired dishes, from appetizers to main courses, and of course, their iconic cheesecakes. At this branch, guests can enjoy a selection of international dishes including pastas, pizzas, seafood, salads, and more. The menu caters well to diverse tastes, including options for vegetarians and those seeking lighter dishes, along with a full kids’ menu. Every dish is generously portioned, a signature of the brand that appeals to groups and families.

Quality of Food

The quality of food at this branch upholds The Cheesecake Factory’s high standards. Starters, such as the avocado egg rolls, are fresh and flavorful. Main courses like the famous Chicken Madeira and Louisiana Chicken Pasta come well-prepared, with balanced flavors and attention to presentation. Ingredients taste fresh, and dishes are consistently well-seasoned. The highlight, of course, is the dessert menu, with over 30 varieties of cheesecakes. The Ultimate Red Velvet Cheesecake is rich and creamy, while the Fresh Strawberry Cheesecake is a lighter option with a refreshing taste.

Service

The service at this location is generally excellent, with staff who are attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable about the menu. Wait times for both seating and food can be a bit long, especially during peak hours, but staff members remain courteous and do their best to keep the experience smooth. Special requests, such as substitutions or dietary needs, are handled with care, and the waitstaff are quick to offer suggestions when needed.

Pricing

The Cheesecake Factory is known for being on the pricier side, and this location is no exception. While dishes are more expensive compared to other dining options in the area, the portions are large and can often be shared. For a full experience, including a main dish and dessert, diners should expect to spend more than usual. However, the quality and portion sizes justify the price, especially for a special occasion or a night out.

Overall Experience

In conclusion, The Cheesecake Factory at Ajdan Walk in Al Khobar provides a memorable dining experience, combining a lively atmosphere, diverse and quality menu options, and attentive service. It’s ideal for a family dinner, celebration, or casual gathering with friends. Despite the high price point and occasional wait time, the restaurant delivers on its promise of flavorful dishes and indulgent desserts, making it a worthwhile visit for anyone seeking a satisfying meal.

Nonetheless, the Khobar Corniche is a must visit, offering a clean, vibrant, and safe haven for relaxation and recreation. Whether you’re there for a leisurely stroll, a family picnic, or to soak in the festive atmosphere, it’s a place that leaves a lasting impression.

The fresh sea breeze and the sound of the waves brought back vivid memories of my earlier visits, and I couldn’t help but compare how the Corniche has grown while still preserving its natural charm. The addition of modern amenities such as cafes, restaurants, and seating areas has elevated the overall experience.

One of the highlights of my visit was observing the skyline, which now boasts a mix of traditional architecture and contemporary structures. The sight of the shimmering water at sunset, paired with the gentle hum of activity around, was absolutely mesmerizing.

The Al-Khobar Corniche is not just a place to admire the beauty of the Arabian Gulf but also a perfect spot for relaxation and family outings. It serves as a bridge between the rich past and the dynamic present, offering something for everyone to enjoy.

For anyone visiting the Eastern Province, this Corniche remains an iconic destination—a place where memories are cherished and new ones are created. I’m so glad I had the chance to revisit it and reconnect with a cherished part of my history.

Review Text:
Disappointed Despite Potential – A Stay That Fell Short of Swiss International Standards

My recent stay at the Swiss International Hotel in Taif left me with mixed feelings. While the hotel exhibits potential through its solid infrastructure and respectful staff, my experience was hindered by issues that should not be present in a hotel carrying the “Swiss International” name.

The Good:
The building itself appears to have been constructed to high standards. The bathroom, in particular, stands out for its spacious design—especially the shower area, which feels generous and well thought out. The bedroom design aligns with what one would expect from a hotel of this caliber—elegant, modern, and functional. The bed provided excellent back support, and the air conditioning was truly outstanding, perhaps one of the best I’ve experienced in any hotel. I also commend the staff for their professionalism; they were consistently respectful, warm, and welcoming.

Where It Falls Short:
Unfortunately, the hotel falters where it matters most: cleanliness and maintenance.
In my first room, the hygiene standards were far below expectations. I encountered clear signs of poor cleaning, such as hair on the bathroom floor, toothpaste residue on the sink, and—most concerningly—unclean marks on the toilet seat. These are not minor oversights; they signal a systemic issue in housekeeping quality control.

To their credit, when I reported the issue to reception, they were quick to respond and offered to move me to another room. While the second room was an improvement, it still showed signs of rushed cleaning (e.g., hair found on the carpet). These details, though small individually, collectively reflect an unsatisfactory cleaning process.

I want to emphasize that this does not appear to be the fault of the staff. Based on conversations and observations, it seems they are working extremely hard, especially given the busy Eid season. In my view, the issue stems from being understaffed, leading to insufficient time spent cleaning each room thoroughly—resulting in superficial rather than deep cleaning.

Other Notes:
•	The rain shower looked promising but had weak water pressure when using hot water, diminishing the overall experience.
•	Pillows were firmer than I prefer, which impacted sleep quality slightly.
•	The room view is unremarkable and doesn’t add much value to the stay.

Conclusion:
While the hotel has many of the elements needed for a premium experience, the severe lapse in cleanliness and maintenance made my stay uncomfortable. I sincerely hope hotel management takes this feedback seriously, as the property has real potential to be one of Taif’s leading hotels if proper staffing and quality assurance measures are implemented. Until then, I cannot confidently recommend it to travelers expecting the high standards typically associated with the Swiss International brand.

1.	Lamb Tajine: Extremely disappointing. It was 80% fat and only 20% meat, with a strong gamey taste that made it hard to enjoy.
2.	Chicken Caesar Salad: Overpriced and underwhelming. We paid restaurant-level prices but received lettuce with mayonnaise, a few pieces of chicken breast, and barely any croutons.
3.	Chicken Tenders: The menu advertised chicken tenders, but we were served grilled chicken instead. It wasn’t what we ordered or expected.
4.	Naan Bread: The naan bread we received looked nothing like the appetizing photos on the menu.
5.	Baklava: This was a huge letdown. It was wet and soggy, with absolutely no crispiness, as though it had been soaking in syrup for hours.
6.	Lasagna: The lasagna had an overpowering cardamom taste, which completely threw off the flavor profile.

Now for the positives:
•	The pizza, pasta, and chicken piccata were absolutely delicious. However, the vegetables served with the chicken piccata were not good and didn’t match the quality of the main dish.

We spent 400 SAR, and while some dishes were enjoyable, the overall experience was disappointing for the price. I’ll be uploading pictures of the receipt, the soggy baklava, the lamb tajine, and other dishes to give an honest visual representation of what we received.

This place has potential but needs major improvements in consistency, quality, and delivering on what the menu promises.

Review Text:
The restaurant has mixed seating with partitions if you require a bit of privacy. The staff are friendly, courteous but you will find it a little difficult placing your order since the menu is in Arabic. The staff can guide you though but I would recommend ordering what we ordered or ask for Mr. Fadel.

1. Beef Kebab Skewers (4 pcs)
2. Chicken with Bone Skewers (2 pcs)
3. Mix Grill Platter
4. Cocktail
5. Hummus
6. Fateela
7. Chicken Pottery
8. Najafey Kebab
9. Grilled Shrimps

The ‘Beef Kebabs’ were outstanding. My wife is a huge fan of chicken but even she was bowled over by the flavours and how succulent it was. You will find this when you order the mixed grill platter.

I had ordered the ‘Grilled Chicken Kebabs’ but they served us the ‘Chicken with Bone Skewers’ instead. I wasn’t disappointed by what I was served and these too were moist. The bone prevents them from drying out and I absolutely loved the spice mix that they used. None of these items are spicy but they do have an edge thanks to the mix they use. You might think it’s spicy but the portions are generous.

The ‘Mix Grill Platter’ offers the best of everything on a single plate, from Grilled Chicken Kebabs to Beef Kebabs, Awsal, Sheesh Tawouk, you name it. We ordered the medium which comes with 6 skewers. You could share this or each one on your own if you are really hungry. If you are going with more than 2 people, go for the large platter.

I can’t describe how succulent and mouth-wateringly delicious the ‘Fateela’ was. We were told to have this grilled beef tenderloin without the bread or Hummus. Seasoned to perfection, the bits of tenderloin is packed with flavour and so tender you’ll barely need to bite into it. I don’t think I have ever enjoyed something as delicious as ‘Fateela’ and I would recommend you make this dish the first thing to order.  It is outstanding!

‘Chicken Pottery’ resembles butter chicken and is oven cooked in a pot with dough acting as a lid to lock in all those flavours. The big difference is that it has cheese and would make an excellent combination with rice if they served it, but we wiped it clean with their in-house bread in no time. It is not as rich, but it is one hearty dish that packs a punch.

The cocktail was just ok and I would stick with the soft drinks.

Finding this place could be a bit tricky so stick to the route mentioned on Google maps. There is also a bit of dirt road to deal with so don’t be alarmed if you don’t find it straight away.

Because most restaurants in Qatif source their meat from local farms in the area and not the mainstream farms.

Review Text:
‘Jawadi Restaurant’ is known for its seafood and you’ll find combinations such as ‘Mahmous & Kanad’ and ‘Mahmous and Hamour’ with the fish complimenting the rice quite well. On it’s own, the rice isn’t the most flavour packed.

We ordered,

‘Mahmous with Hamour’- SR. 49
‘Prawn Kabsa’ - SR. 49
‘Grilled Aroosa’ ( 1 1/2 KG) - SR. 68

Without the fish, Mahmous is extremely subtle though I enjoyed this more than the Sayadiyah rice. The Hamour comes fried and is quite delicate and packing a ton of flavour. I would love to know what they are marinating the fish with.

The highlight of the evening had to be the ‘Prawn Kabsa’. I haven’t had this much flavour from a prawn and rice based dish and these guys really pulled it off. The rice had absorbed the richness of the prawn gravy and it was so tasty that we ordered another plate.

The ‘Grilled Aroosa’ was a bargain for SR. 68. Getting it right and not overcooking the fish is a feat they accomplished quite successfully. We were already quite full at this point but wasted no time in wiping the bones clean of any flesh.

Jawadi is a must visit if you are in Qatif and I guarantee you won’t regret it.

Place Name: Asador de Aranda | Spanish Restaurant | Laysen Valley
Review Text:
Spanish restaurant in Riyadh.

Order: A5 wagyu, entrecote, wagyu empanadas, potatas bravas, chicken croquettes, octopus

Location: I don't know Riyadh very well but it is in a very high end area and valet parking is available. 5/5

Venue: Welcoming decor, very unpretentious and comfortable.  4.5/5

Service: Saudi Arabia sets the bar and gold standard for service in general.  Friendly and hospitable. Knowledgeable wait staff. 5/5

Food:  The appetizers were a lovely way to start the meal foreshadowing the main dishes to come.  Tasty bits to tantalize the taste buds.  From the potato bravas, to the croquettes and empanadas, each bite as marvelous.

The octopus was cooked to perfection.  My good friend who doesn't enjoy seafood thought it was great.   Tender not chewy.

Steaks definitely were among the best I had in recent years.  I dine at higher end steak restaurants regularly and frequently.  My jaw dropped in amazement of how well prepared the steaks were.  A5 wagyu was delightfully succulent.  Small explosions of umami pleasure as it melts in your mouth. The entrecote was a very ideal steak.   Rich flavor, very well seasoned and addictive delicious.   9.3 Wagyu, 9.1 Entrecote.  Unforgettable meal.

Review Text:
A Taste of Lebanon in the Heart of Saudi

Finding an authentic Lebanese dining experience outside of Lebanon can be a challenge, but Burj Al Hamam in Saudi Arabia proves that great food knows no borders. Renowned for its dedication to traditional recipes, high-quality ingredients, and warm hospitality, this restaurant delivers an unforgettable journey through the heart of Lebanese cuisine.

From the moment I stepped inside, I was greeted with the kind of hospitality that makes Middle Eastern dining so special. The ambiance was elegant yet inviting, with a mix of modern sophistication and traditional Lebanese charm. Soft Arabic music played in the background, setting the perfect mood for a relaxed and immersive experience.

The meal began with an impressive spread of mezze, the cornerstone of Lebanese cuisine. The Hummus was silky smooth, with the perfect balance of tahini and lemon, while the Baba Ghanoush had a delicious smokiness that elevated its creamy texture. The Tabbouleh, bursting with fresh parsley, tomatoes, and zesty lemon, was one of the best I’ve ever had—light, refreshing, and perfectly seasoned.

The Shish Taouk was beautifully marinated, tender, and juicy, while the Lamb Kofta delivered rich, spiced flavours that melted in the mouth. The Mashawi platter, featuring grilled meats with a side of warm, pillowy Khobz, was an absolute standout, offering a true taste of Lebanon’s renowned barbecue tradition.

For seafood lovers, the Sayadieh—a fragrant, spiced rice dish topped with perfectly cooked fish—was a revelation. The caramelised onions and subtle blend of spices gave it incredible depth, making every bite a delight.

No Lebanese feast is complete without dessert, and Burj Al Hamam delivered in spectacular fashion. The Knafeh, a crispy, golden pastry filled with gooey, sweet cheese and drizzled with orange blossom syrup, was indulgent and utterly delicious. Paired with a cup of Lebanese coffee, it was the perfect way to end an exceptional meal.

Beyond the incredible food, what made this experience so memorable was the impeccable service. The staff were attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about Lebanese cuisine. Every dish was presented with care, and the team was more than happy to recommend pairings and share insights into the rich culinary heritage of Lebanon.

Whether you’re a long-time lover of Lebanese food or a newcomer to this vibrant cuisine, Burj Al Hamam is a must-visit in Saudi Arabia. It’s a place where tradition meets excellence, where every dish tells a story, and where the spirit of Lebanese hospitality shines through in every detail. A dining experience I won’t soon forget.

Overall it was a lovely experience. 10/10 would recommend and we can't wait to come back for the other showings.

Review Text:
A Winter Wonderland in the Desert: Snow City, Al Othaim Mall

If you’re looking for a fun and unique family adventure in Riyadh, Snow City at Al Othaim Mall is a must-visit. As a family living in the desert, we couldn’t resist the idea of stepping into a winter wonderland for a couple of hours—and it did not disappoint!

A Personal, Exclusive Experience…
We visited Snow City during a quiet time and had the entire park to ourselves, which made the experience feel intimate and extra special. Spending two hours surrounded by snow and engaging in a variety of activities turned out to be the perfect amount of time. At 169 SAR per person, I initially thought it was a little pricey for a family of four, but as we explored ride after ride, it became clear that the experience was worth every riyal.

Thrills for Everyone…
Snow City has a great mix of activities for kids and adults alike. The rides and slides are not just for small children; they’re designed to be exciting and memorable for all ages. From tobogganing to riding rubber rings and even navigating a luge, every slide offered something new. My daughters especially loved the snow plough bumper cars and the snowmobiles—watching them zoom around with big smiles on their faces was a highlight for me.

Another standout activity was the climbing wall. Unlike a traditional rock wall, this one had handle-style grips, making it accessible to everyone. Reaching the top and rappelling down with the auto-belay was thrilling, and we all had multiple turns. It’s a little more physical than you might expect—climbing, crawling, and sliding keep you active—but that only added to the fun.

Impeccable Facilities…
The attention to cleanliness and organization was impressive. Snow suits, boots, gloves, and helmets were provided and looked brand new. Even the socks they gave us were fresh out of the package! The changing rooms were spotless, and the equipment inside the park was clearly well-maintained. The snow itself was clean and fluffy—perfect for snowball fights and making snow angels.

Fantastic Staff and Service…
The staff truly made our experience unforgettable. Because the park was empty, they gave us their full attention, ensuring we felt welcome, safe, and well looked after. They carefully explained the rules for each activity, especially the climbing wall, and their cheerful demeanor made the experience even more enjoyable. The kids felt especially special thanks to their kindness and encouragement.

A Unique Desert Escape…
Snow City offers a unique escape from the desert heat. Playing in the snow, exploring the igloo maze, and having a snowball fight felt surreal—and so much fun. By the end of the two hours, we were all tired, exhilarated, and a little chilly, but we left with warm hearts and great memories.

Tips for Visiting…
We recommend visiting during quieter times to fully enjoy the park without crowds. We’ve been during both the Christmas holidays and Ramadan, and both visits were equally peaceful. Look out for special offers during the year to save on ticket prices.

While 169 SAR per person might seem steep at first, the exclusive feel, pristine facilities, and variety of activities made it worthwhile. For us, two hours was just the right amount of time before toes started freezing!

Final Thoughts…
Snow City is perfect for families with kids around 8-11 years old, but adults will have plenty of fun too. It’s an active, exhilarating experience that offers something rare and special in Riyadh—a chance to play in the snow in the middle of the desert.

We walked away with a shared family memory that we’ll cherish for years. For anyone looking for a fun, active, and memorable day out, Snow City is a winter wonderland worth exploring.

One of the worst hotel experiences we’ve ever had.

•	The hotel falsely advertises itself as a beachfront resort, but there is no beach access whatsoever.
•	The pool is not accessible for elderly or disabled guests — it has a massive step (around 2x a normal height) and no bannister.

On top of that, he had such strong body odour that it lingered in the room long after he left, adding even more discomfort to an already awful situation.

When I expressed to the receptionist how disgraceful the entire experience had been-and hung up due to my emotional distress- she proceeded to call our room four more times. When my mother answered, she was rudely told to “tell your daughter…” — an incredibly unprofessional and patronising way to speak to paying guests.

To summarise:
•	Filthy room and dirty, dumped bedding
•	Rotten food served
•	False advertising of beach access
•	No accessibility for disabled guests
•	Broken promises, poor communication, and disrespectful staff
•	Uncomfortable and invasive interactions with staff
•	Forced to stay one night, cut our trip short, and paid to change our flights just to leave

Review Text:
Al Rashid Mall in Jazan is a relatively small mall compared to others in the region, and it has limited options for shopping and dining. When visiting, I noticed that the variety of shopping brands is quite restricted, making it challenging for those looking for diverse retail experiences. Popular and trendy brands that you would typically expect in a mall are missing, leaving the shopping options underwhelming.
The food court is another area where the mall falls short. It only has four food brands, which means there isn’t much choice when it comes to dining. For families or individuals who enjoy exploring different cuisines or food options during their shopping trips, this can be disappointing. The lack of variety also makes it difficult for the mall to cater to the tastes of a wide range of visitors.
On a positive note, the mall is clean and well-maintained, with a comfortable atmosphere.
